review_notes: I read the whole of WeakHull.lean. I also listed the declarations in ConvexFlag/Basic.lean (ConvexFlag, Point, LinearFunction, ConvexCombination, convexHull, IsProjectionOf) to see what the file builds on. The file defines two things: `weakConvexHull`, and `WeaklyConvexPosition` (the analogue of Mathlib's `ConvexIndependent`, but for the weak hull of a flag). `weakConvexHull` is the set of points that no flag-linear functional can separate strictly from S. That is specific to the partially-defined flag points and functionals of this development. It is not the same as Mathlib's `convexHull`, or any other Mathlib concept, because evaluation is only partial (`EvaluableAt`). The other results are basic hull facts (extensive, monotone, absorbing, idempotent) and the Proposition 3.11 characterization. The proof of that characterization uses Mathlib directly: `_root_.convexHull`, `geometric_hahn_banach_closed_point`, `mem_convexHull_iff_exists_fintype` and `Finset.affineCombination`. The file introduces no parallel version of any of these. I did not search Mathlib exhaustively for a generic closure-operator or "hull relative to a family of functionals" structure that `weakConvexHull` could be rephrased through. I found no concrete duplicated API or repeated conversions that would justify a finding, so I abstain.
